Name: Demographics
Analysis Questions: What is the size, distribution, structure, and dynamics of the population (including birth rates, death rates, and migration patterns)? How do fertility, mortality, migration, and social and economic factors shape population change over time? What are the implications of these demographic changes for public health, education, employment, social welfare, and environmental sustainability?

Name: Political
Analysis Questions: What is the overall structure of government and decision-making processes at local, national, and international levels, and how has the political system evolved over time? How is power competed for and how are resources and values allocated within society? What roles do elections, political parties, interest groups, lobbying, and social movements play, and how do negotiations, compromise, and conflict resolution operate among groups with different interests?

Name: Economy
Analysis Questions: What is the structure of production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services? How do individuals, businesses, and governments allocate resources to meet needs and wants? How do markets operate, how are prices determined, and how do supply and demand interact? What are the key economic behaviours of firms, households, and governments and their consequences for the economy as a whole?

Name: Socio culture
Analysis Questions: What are the main social norms, institutions, and structures that shape how people interact and form identities? What shared beliefs, practices, customs, and traditions influence perspectives, behaviours, and lifestyles? How are social groups defined (including ethnic, minority, and gender groups), and how have their roles and statuses evolved? How do socio-cultural factors influence social inequality, discrimination, cohesion, and diversity?

Name: Security
Analysis Questions: What are the main security, stability, and conflict risks, and how do they impact different social groups and regions?

Name: Legal and policy
Analysis Questions: What are the key legal frameworks and policies governing the country, and what trends have emerged in recent years?

Name: Infrastructure & technology
Analysis Questions: How has technological adoption and cybersecurity evolved, and what impact has it had on the social and economic landscape?

Name: Environment
Analysis Questions: What are the key climate and environmental factors affecting the country, including natural conditions and processes (atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere, cryosphere, biosphere) and human activities that influence or are influenced by them? How do these factors determine climate, climate zones, land cover, natural resources, climate change, and the seasonal agricultural calendar, and how have they changed over the past decade?

Name: Humanitarian Coordination
Analysis Questions: What governmental and humanitarian coordination structures and mechanisms are in place to respond to crises or emergencies? What procedures and regulations ensure coordinated, coherent, and principled approaches to the response? How do these arrangements seek to improve effectiveness through greater predictability, accountability, and partnership?

Name: Displacement
Analysis Questions: What is the current total number of internally displaced people, refugees, returnees and asylum seekers? What are the main geographical areas they come from? What are the main geographical areas they displaced to? What are the main settings they use (camps, private accommodation, hosted by relatives, collective centres, etc.)? How many time in average have displaced families been displaced? What is the average duration of displacement? What are the main challenges faced by the displaced population regarding social integration in the area of diaplacement, e.g. Tensions with local communities, discrimination, unequal access to job opportunities, etc?

Name: Shock-Event
Analysis Questions: What are the main characteristics of the disaster/shock/event, i.e. Type of shock, intensity, characteristics, locations affected, etc.? What pre existing measures, policies or mechanisms mitigated the intensity of the disaster and its impact on population and services?

Name: Humanitarian Access
Analysis Questions: How many of the people affected are currently facing moderate or severe humanitarian access barriers? What are the main humanitarian access barriers faced by humanitarian actors when planning or conducting humanitarian response? What are the main humanitarian access barriers faced by the affected population when planning or attempting to access humanitarian assistance, Information and communication constraints.

Name: Agriculture
Analysis Questions: What are the shock-related impacts on crops, livestock, productive assets, markets, inputs, and land access? What are the resulting humanitarian conditions and coping strategies? What are the principal risks, vulnerabilities, and their severity?

Name: Education
Analysis Questions: What are the impacts on schools, teachers, learning continuity, and learning outcomes? What are the resulting access, availability, quality, and coping conditions? What are the principal risks and vulnerabilities facing learners, including girls and displaced children?

Name: Food Security
Analysis Questions: What are the impacts on production, income, markets, and household food access? What are the resulting food availability, access, utilisation, deprivation, and coping strategies? What are the principal acute food insecurity risks, vulnerabilities, and their severity?

Name: Health
Analysis Questions: What are the impacts on facilities, care pathways, services, and disease burden? What are the resulting access, availability, quality, wellbeing, and coping conditions? What are the principal health risks, vulnerabilities, and their severity?

Name: Livelihoods
Analysis Questions: What are the impacts on employment, income, productive assets, and markets? What are the resulting access to work, income, debt, and coping conditions? What are the principal livelihood risks, vulnerabilities, and their severity?

Name: Logistics
Analysis Questions: What are the impacts on roads, ports, warehouses, and supply chains? What are the resulting transport, storage, fuel, and supply constraints? What are the principal pipeline, seasonal-access, and corridor-security risks and their severity?

Name: Nutrition
Analysis Questions: What are the shock-related changes in nutrition outcomes and service delivery? What are the resulting access, food-quality, feeding-practice, wellbeing, and coping conditions? What are the principal acute malnutrition, infant-feeding, and micronutrient risks and their severity?

Name: Protection
Analysis Questions: What are the violence, coercion, rights, documentation, legal-status, and freedom-of-movement impacts? What are the resulting safety, service-access, and coping conditions? What are the principal protection risks, vulnerabilities, and their severity?

Name: Shelter
Analysis Questions: What are the housing damage, destruction, overcrowding, and eviction impacts? What are the resulting shelter adequacy, privacy, durability, rental, hosting, and coping conditions? What are the principal exposure and tenure risks, vulnerabilities, and their severity?

Name: WASH
Analysis Questions: What are the impacts on water and sanitation systems and contamination? What are the resulting water quantity, quality, access, sanitation, hygiene, and coping conditions? What are the principal waterborne-disease, scarcity, and unsafe-sanitation risks and their severity?
